dedupe_keys.name: understanding the transport and fate of ejected sewer sediments during urban flood events

description: Martins, Ricardo at RISCO - research center for risks and sustainability in construction publishes experimental observations of sediment released from surcharging sewers into shallow urban flooding through Co-UDlabs. The Martins transnational-access campaign examines sediment transport out of drainage infrastructure and subsequent deposition on the flooded surface. Six DAT data-file descriptors accompany a storage report. Coverage is the Sheffield A/B flume experimental facility; full test dates and dimensional scale are not stated. Zenodo provides six DAT files and a PDF report with free access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. These observations support the source-defined drainage measurement, physical-model or simulation activity. Related Co-UDlabs experiments describe other assets and test conditions; they are not assumed to be independent or interchangeable measurements. A limitation is the short description does not define DAT columns, sediment classes, units or individual test boundary conditions. Only native metadata and file descriptors were read; no data values, archive, code or report body was obtained.
